items.title: A centre whose orbit meets the discontinuities lies in a non-trivial connection
items.author: Przemyslaw Berk; Frank Trujillo
items.work: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 652-670: for a symmetric interval exchange transformation, if some iterate of a centre is an endpoint of a continuity interval then the shifted backward iterate of that centre is again an endpoint, with the index shifted by one, and the centre lies in a non-trivial connection. The signature is already delicate, because the shift by the indicator of the case beta equal to one half and the direction of the shift of the index both depend on the sign of the iterate. The proof (source lines 672-682) separates the degenerate exponent, rewrites the hypothesis through the formula for backward iterates of centres, and then has to exclude the special index before the endpoint identity can be applied. The statement records the two displayed formulas and the connection conclusion only.
